concept: A poll's margin of error shrinks with the square root of the sample size, so halving it costs 4x the people.

misconceptions.label: Twice the people, half the error
misconceptions.why_tempting: More data should shrink error in step.
misconceptions.refutation: Error shrinks with the square root of sample size: half the error takes 4x the people (about 4,000).
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Precision needs huge samples
misconceptions.why_tempting: Polls of millions seem necessary for precision.
misconceptions.refutation: Going from 1,000 to 4,000 people already halves the error.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

items.prompt: A poll of 1,000 people has a margin of error of about 3.1%. About how many people do you need for 1.55%?

extremes.watch: With z = 1 (a looser ±1 standard error) you need only about 1,041 people for ±1.55%.
With z = 3 (3 standard errors wide) you need about 9,365 people.
